en.title: Lanterns Trailer Drops: Hal Jordan and John Stewart Tackle a Nebraska Mystery
en.summary: The first trailer for HBO Max's upcoming DC series, Lanterns, has arrived, revealing a surprising shift from cosmic battles to a grounded mystery in the heartland. Hal Jordan and John Stewart find themselves investigating more than just alien threats.
en.body:
The DC Universe on TV is undergoing a significant transformation under the stewardship of **James Gunn** and **Peter Safran**, and the latest glimpse comes from the **Lanterns** trailer. While fans might expect intergalactic dogfights and universe-saving heroics from a series focused on the Green Lantern Corps, the initial footage teases a much more intimate and chilling narrative. Instead of battling cosmic warlords, **Hal Jordan** (played by **Kyle Chandler**) and his new recruit **John Stewart** (portrayed by **Aaron Pierre**) find themselves drawn into a perplexing mystery unfolding in rural Nebraska.

The trailer reveals that the core of the story will involve the enigmatic Manhunters, a sinister force with a complex history within the Green Lantern lore. This shift from the vastness of space to the seemingly ordinary setting of a small town promises a unique blend of sci-fi intrigue and grounded detective procedural. The series co-creators, **Damon Lindelof**, **Chris Mundy**, and **Tom King**, appear to be leaning into a narrative that explores the human element of these iconic cosmic protectors, forcing them to confront a threat that is both deeply personal and disturbingly familiar.

## A Chilling Nebraska Mystery

The ensemble cast surrounding **Chandler** and **Pierre** hints at the depth of this mystery. **Kelly Macdonald** stars as Kerry, a determined local cop who becomes entangled with the Lanterns' investigation. **Garret Dillahunt** plays William Macon, a charismatic but conspiracy-minded cowboy, whose wife is portrayed by **Poorna Jagannathan**. These characters suggest that the Nebraska setting is not merely a backdrop but integral to the unfolding conspiracy. The dynamic between **Hal** and **John** is also a focal point, with the trailer hinting at initial friction and mentorship as **Hal** grapples with training **John**, seeing him as a potential replacement rather than a partner.

> "Hal sees his new pal as a replacement, not as a backup." — **Sinestro** (as relayed in the trailer)

This particular line, spoken by **Ulrich Thomsen**'s **Sinestro**, adds a layer of internal conflict to **Hal Jordan**'s character, suggesting his journey will involve more than just solving the Manhunter case. The tease of **Nathan Fillion** reprising his role as **Guy Gardner** also promises a connection to the wider DC Universe, but the immediate focus remains on the Nebraska mystery.

## Fan Expectations and Future Implications

The decision to ground the **Lanterns** series in a terrestrial mystery has certainly piqued the interest of fans. While the Green Lanterns are known for their epic cosmic adventures, this approach allows for a deeper exploration of their characters and their interactions with the human world. The inclusion of **John Stewart** in the upcoming **Superman** sequel, **Man of Tomorrow**, confirms his importance to the new DC Universe, but the fate of **Hal Jordan** remains a significant question mark. The trailer itself seems to pose the question of whether **Hal** will survive the events of the series, adding a layer of suspense that is sure to keep viewers engaged.

## What's Next

Fans can officially dive into the mystery when **Lanterns** premieres on HBO Max on August 16. The trailer has set the stage for a compelling narrative that blends familiar DC heroes with an unexpected, grounded thriller. Viewers should prepare for a journey that promises both thrilling action and intricate character development.

content_raw: The CW’s Arrowverse may be over, but under the rule of James Gunn and Peter Safran, the DC Universe on TV continues to expand on HBO Max. After Peacemaker and the animated Creature Commandos, the latest entrant,   Lanterns, w ill premiere next month. To tease the plot and the franchise’s future, stars Kyle Chandler, Aaron Pierre, Poorna Jagannathan, and Garret Dillahunt, as well as co-creators Damon Lindelof, Chris Mundy, and Tom King , took to the San Diego Comic-Con stage on July 24. Lanterns follows former test pilot Hal Jordan (Chandler), who begins training new Green Lantern Corps recruit John Stewart (Pierre). However, they get caught up not in a massive cosmic battle, but in a chilling mystery in Nebraska involving Manhunters. The case puts them directly in the path of a dogged local cop, Kerry (Kelly Macdonald), and a charming but conspiracy-minded cowboy, William Macon (Dillahunt). Jagannathan stars as William’s wife, while Nathan Fillion is set to reprise his Superman role as bowl-cut emissary Guy Gardner. The ensemble also features Jason Ritter and Nicole Ari Parker.  The SDCC-released trailer promises plenty of banter between Hal and John. It also reveals that Hal sees his new pal as a replacement, not as a backup, according to what he tells his mentor, Sinestro (Ulrich Thomsen).  As for the other characters’ futures, it’s already confirmed that Pierre’s John Stewart will appear in next year’s Superman sequel, Man Of Tomorrow .
